title: feat(editor): add getSelectedText(), multi-line list toggle, and atomic replaceRange
body:
## Summary / 摘要

Add `getSelectedText()` and `replaceRange()` to `EditorAPI`, and fix multi-line list toggle to operate on the full selection range with atomic undo.

## Motivation / 背景与动机

Roadmap: #1 (多行列表切换, P1), #5 (getSelectedText() API, P0), #8 (undo/redo 分组, P1)  
OpenSpec change: `openspec/changes/add-selection-api/`

## Changes / 变更内容

**packages/core:**
- Add `getSelectedText(): string` and `replaceRange(from, to, insert, selection?, opts?)` to `EditorAPI`

**packages/plugin-toolbar:**
- Introduce `getLinesInRange()` + refactor `applyLines()` to use `replaceRange` (single CM6 transaction)
- Fix `toggleOrderedList` / `toggleUnorderedList` to operate on full anchor/head range

**openspec/:**
- Add `changes/add-selection-api/` with `proposal.md`, `tasks.md`, spec deltas for `editor-core` and `plugin-toolbar`

## Testing / 测试

```bash
pnpm test -- packages/core packages/plugin-toolbar
# 191 passed, 0 failures
```

## Checklist / 自检清单

- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits
- [x] Public API changes update README / types — EditorAPI updated with full TSDoc
- [x] New capability → OpenSpec linked — `openspec/changes/add-selection-api/`
- [x] No secrets committed

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+## Roadmap items
+
+Closes roadmap #1 (多行列表切换, P1), #5 (`getSelectedText()` API, P0), and #8 (undo/redo 分组, P1).
+
+## Problem
+
+`toggleOrderedList` and `toggleUnorderedList` read only `anchor` from
+the current selection, silently ignoring `head`. Any multi-line
+selection was collapsed to a single-line operation — selecting three
+lines and pressing the list button mutated only the anchor line.
+
+`getSelectedText()` was absent from `EditorAPI`, forcing every caller
+to manually reconstruct the selected string from raw `anchor`/`head`
+coordinates and a full `getDocument()` call.
+
+## Solution
+
+Unified the selection model from cursor-only to full range across the
+list toggle commands. `getSelectedText()` exposes the derived value at
+the correct abstraction boundary, consistent with how `getSelection()`
+and `replaceSelection()` already operate.
+
+Both changes share a root cause: list commands assumed cursor-only positions where the API already exposes a full selection range. This PR corrects that assumption consistently across core and formatting logic.
+
+## Changes
+
+- **core**: add `getSelectedText(): string` to `EditorAPI` (P0 roadmap item)
+- **core**: add `replaceRange(from, to, insert, selection?, opts?)` to `EditorAPI` — a narrow atomic primitive that replaces a substring and optionally repositions the cursor in one CM6 transaction (one undo entry)
+- **plugin-toolbar**: introduce `getLinesInRange()` and `applyLines()` to replace the single-cursor assumption in both list toggle functions; `applyLines` uses `replaceRange` so the entire toggle is a single undo entry
+
+## Scope boundary
+
+Only list commands (`toggleOrderedList`, `toggleUnorderedList`) are migrated to range-aware selection. `toggleHeading` and `toggleBlockquote` remain cursor-based intentionally: Markdown headings have no multi-line form, and blockquote toggling conventionally targets the current paragraph. Extending those to range-based would change their semantics, not fix them.
+
+## Toggle semantics (multi-line)
+
+| State | Result |
+|---|---|
+| All selected lines already marked | Remove markers (toggle off) |
+| Any line unmarked | Add markers to all (mixed → on) |
+| Selection ends at column 0 of next line | Next line excluded (standard convention) |
+| Reversed selection (head < anchor) | Normalized via `Math.min`/`Math.max` |
+
+Mixed → on matches the behaviour of VS Code and Obsidian.
+
+## Atomic undo
+
+The previous implementation called `setDocument` then `setSelection` — two CM6 dispatches, two undo entries. After toggling three lines into a list, pressing Ctrl+Z once reverted only the selection move, leaving the document in a mangled half-toggled state.
+
+`replaceRange` is the fix: it emits a single transaction containing both the range edit and the resulting selection, so one Ctrl+Z fully reverts the operation. This is the same pattern already used by `markdown-keymap.ts` and `markdown-autopair.ts` inside core.
+
+**Why a new primitive instead of extending existing methods:**
+- `setDocument` is semantically wrong for range edits — its name and docs imply whole-document replacement.
+- Exposing raw `dispatch({ changes, selection })` would leak CM6's transaction shape into the framework-agnostic `EditorAPI` contract.
+
+**Bounds contract:** callers pass pre-edit doc coordinates. CM6 throws `RangeError` on out-of-bounds offsets — the same trust model `setSelection` already uses. No double validation is performed in this layer.
+
+**Behavior preservation:** the atomic dispatch changes only the *grouping* of edits in undo history. Visible document state, cursor position, and `scrollIntoView` behavior are identical to before. Existing tests that do not touch undo all pass unchanged.
+
+## Tests
+
+191 passing, 0 failures (packages/core + packages/plugin-toolbar).
+
+New cases:
+- `getSelectedText`: collapsed cursor, forward selection, reversed selection, multi-line
+- List toggles: single-line backward compat, multi-line add/remove, mixed state, reversed selection, column-0 boundary, cross-marker replacement (UL↔OL)
+- Atomic undo (7 cases): single undo fully reverts multi-line toggle; redo recovers in one step; reversed selection composes correctly with undo; collapsed cursor path; undo→redo→undo round-trip stability
+- **Case 4 is the load-bearing regression guard**: `multi-line toggle → undo → second undo() returns false` fails on the old two-dispatch code and passes only after the `replaceRange` refactor. Any future change to `applyLines` that re-splits the dispatch will turn this test red.
